definition: a proposed explanation that has yet to be tested
example: The researchers set out to test the hypothesis that sleep improves memory.

definition: a scientific test carried out to discover or prove something
example: The experiment was repeated three times to make sure the results were consistent.

definition: based on observation or experience rather than theory alone
example: There is little empirical evidence to support the claim that the treatment is effective.

definition: the system of methods used in a particular study or field
example: The study's methodology was criticised because the sample was too small.

definition: a factor in an experiment that can change or be changed
example: The scientists changed only one variable at a time to see its effect.

definition: a set of participants in an experiment who do not receive the treatment being tested
example: The control group received a harmless placebo, so their results could be compared with those of the test group.

definition: the number of people or items studied in a piece of research
example: Because the sample size was small, the findings may not apply to the wider population.

definition: the checking of research by other experts before it is published
example: Peer review helps to ensure that published studies meet accepted standards.

definition: an important discovery or development that solves a problem
example: Scientists announced a breakthrough in the search for a cure for the disease.

definition: the act of finding something new or the thing found
example: The discovery of penicillin transformed the treatment of infections.

definition: the results of a piece of research
example: The findings suggest that regular exercise slows the ageing of the brain.

definition: a set of ideas intended to explain facts or events
example: Einstein's theory of relativity changed the way scientists understand time and space.

definition: to prove that something is correct or true
example: Further experiments are needed to validate these early results.

definition: to repeat a study or experiment and obtain the same results
example: Other teams have failed to replicate the results, which casts doubt on the claim.

definition: able to be repeated with the same results
example: For research to be trusted, its results must be reproducible by independent teams.

definition: something that differs from what is normal or expected
example: The anomaly in the data led the team to re-examine their equipment.

definition: the careful watching of something in order to learn about it
example: Darwin's observation of finches on the islands helped to shape his theory.

definition: a connection between two things that vary together
example: Researchers found a strong correlation between hours of sleep and exam performance.

definition: the relationship in which one event brings about another
example: Correlation does not necessarily imply causation, so further tests are required.

definition: to suggest an explanation that has not yet been proved
example: Researchers hypothesise that the species migrated across the land bridge.

definition: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence
example: Scientists deduce the age of a rock by measuring the decay of its minerals.

definition: to form an opinion from evidence rather than direct statements
example: We can infer from the data that temperatures were higher in the region a million years ago.

definition: to measure or express something as a number
example: It is difficult to quantify the benefits of basic research.

definition: to adjust an instrument so that its readings are accurate
example: Technicians must calibrate the instruments carefully before each new measurement is taken.

definition: a room or building equipped for scientific experiments
example: The vaccine was developed in a laboratory before being tested on volunteers.

definition: a sample of an animal, plant or substance used for study
example: The museum keeps thousands of preserved specimens collected over two centuries.

definition: an instrument that makes very small things look larger
paraphrases: a device for viewing tiny objects
example: Bacteria are too small to be seen without a microscope.

definition: an instrument that makes distant objects look nearer and larger
paraphrases: a viewing instrument for distant objects
example: The new telescope can detect light from stars that formed billions of years ago.

definition: an extremely small piece of matter
example: Physicists use huge machines to make particles collide at high speed.

definition: the smallest unit of a chemical compound, made of atoms
example: A water molecule consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

definition: the complete set of genetic material in an organism
example: Scientists completed the sequencing of the human genome in 2003.

definition: a unit of heredity that carries instructions for a characteristic
example: A single faulty gene can cause a serious inherited disease.

definition: a change in the genetic material of a living thing
example: A tiny mutation in the virus made it much easier to spread.

definition: the gradual change of living things over many generations
example: The evolution of birds from dinosaurs is supported by many fossil discoveries.

definition: a living thing, especially a very small one
example: Every organism, however small, depends on other living things for survival.

definition: the remains of a plant or animal preserved in rock
example: The fossil provides clear evidence that the creature lived over a hundred million years ago.

definition: the smallest basic unit of living things
example: The body is made of trillions of cells, each carrying out a particular task.

definition: a research study in which a new treatment is tested on human volunteers
paraphrases: a test of a treatment on patients
example: The drug is being tested in a clinical trial involving two thousand patients.

definition: introducing new ideas or methods for the first time
paraphrases: innovative and first of its kind
example: The pioneering work of the 1950s laid the foundations for modern genetics.

definition: using the newest and most advanced ideas or methods
example: The laboratory uses cutting-edge equipment to study individual atoms.

definition: new and very important, changing the way something is done
example: The groundbreaking study overturned decades of accepted belief about the cause of the disease.

definition: money provided for a particular purpose such as research
example: Cuts in public funding have forced several research projects to close.

definition: a sum of money given for a particular purpose such as research
example: The team received a grant of two million pounds to study ocean currents.

definition: a person who carries out detailed study to discover new information
example: A team of researchers spent five years studying the habits of the animals.

definition: a person who has studied a subject in great depth
example: The scholar published more than fifty articles on the history of mathematics.

definition: careful and critical examination
example: Claims of this kind must withstand rigorous scientific scrutiny.

definition: done carefully and thoroughly, with great attention to detail
example: All new medicines undergo rigorous testing before they reach the market.

definition: strong and unlikely to fail or be proved wrong
example: The conclusions are supported by robust evidence from several independent studies.

definition: able to be believed or trusted
example: The scientist's claim is credible because it is backed by repeated experiments.

definition: able to be trusted to give consistent results
example: Online surveys are quick, but their results are not always reliable.

definition: an unfair preference that affects how something is judged
example: Researchers must guard against bias when they interpret their own results.

definition: relating to principles of right and wrong behaviour
example: Testing on animals raises serious ethical questions for many people.

definition: causing public disagreement or argument
example: The use of human embryos in research remains highly controversial.

definition: the process of producing an identical copy of a living thing
example: The cloning of a sheep in 1996 sparked a worldwide debate about ethics.

definition: the deliberate alteration of the genes of a living thing
example: Genetic engineering has produced crops that can resist disease.

definition: a basic cell that can develop into many different types of cell
paraphrases: a cell able to become other cell types
example: Stem cell research offers hope for treating injuries that were once considered permanent.

definition: the force that pulls objects towards each other, especially towards the Earth
example: Astronauts must exercise daily because the body weakens in conditions of low gravity.

definition: the curved path of an object moving around a planet or star
paraphrases: a circular path around a body
example: The satellite remains in orbit about four hundred kilometres above the Earth.

definition: a very large group of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity
example: Our galaxy contains hundreds of billions of stars.

definition: all of space and everything that exists in it
example: Astronomers believe the universe began with a massive explosion about fourteen billion years ago.

definition: a scientist who studies stars, planets and other objects in space
example: The astronomer spent years observing a faint star that changed brightness at regular intervals.

definition: a scientist who studies matter, energy and the forces between them
paraphrases: a scientist of matter and energy
example: The physicist won a prize for explaining how light behaves at very small scales.

definition: a scientist who studies living things
example: The biologist spent a year in the rainforest recording the behaviour of insects.

definition: a chemical process in which substances change into other substances
example: When the two liquids are mixed, a violent reaction takes place.

definition: a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction, or something that causes change
example: The discovery acted as a catalyst for a whole new field of research.

definition: a substance made of two or more elements chemically joined
example: Water is a compound formed from hydrogen and oxygen.

definition: energy sent out as waves or particles, such as light or X-rays
example: Prolonged exposure to radiation can damage living tissue.

definition: a fact or event that can be observed, especially something unusual
example: The northern lights are a natural phenomenon caused by particles from the sun.

definition: a fundamental change in the basic ideas of a subject
example: The discovery of DNA brought about a paradigm shift in the study of life.

definition: a method of learning by trying different ways until one works
collocations: a process of trial and error
example: Many early inventions were developed through trial and error rather than theory.

definition: the range within which a measurement might be wrong
collocations: allow for a margin of error
example: Opinion polls always carry a margin of error of a few percentage points.

definition: unlikely to have happened by chance alone, according to a mathematical test
example: The difference between the two groups was statistically significant.

definition: proving something beyond doubt
example: There is no conclusive proof that the drug is responsible for the side effects.

definition: not certain or final, and open to change
example: The scientists reached a tentative conclusion but warned that more work was needed.

definition: not leading to a firm result
example: The results of the trial were inconclusive, so a larger study was planned.

definition: to solve or understand something complicated
example: Scientists are slowly beginning to unravel the mystery of how the brain stores memories.

definition: to help explain something not previously understood
example: The discovery of the ancient tools sheds light on how early humans lived.

definition: an important stage or event in a process
example: The first landing on the moon was a milestone in human exploration.

definition: based on a possible situation rather than a proven fact
example: The model describes a hypothetical planet with conditions similar to those on Earth.
